title: History Lec 4
summary: Chandragupta I (319-335 AD) took the title Maharajadhiraja; Samudragupta 335-375 AD; Chandragupta II 380-415 AD
Chandragupta II defeated the Shakas and took the title Vikramaditya; Fa-Hien visited in his reign, Hiuen Tsang in Harsha's reign
Mehrauli Iron Pillar (7.2 m) is linked to Chandragupta II; Navaratnas: Kalidasa, Varahamihira, Amarasimha (lexicographer), Shanku (architect), Dhanvantari (physician), Vetalabhatta
The Prayag Prashasti was composed by Harishena in praise of Samudragupta; Samudragupta is shown playing the veena on coins; V. A. Smith called him the 'Napoleon of India'
Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty: capital Thanesar, Prabhakaravardhana the first notable ruler (580-605); Harsha 606-647 AD, later capital Kannauj
Rajyashri married the Maukhari Grahavarman; Devagupta (Malwa) killed Grahavarman and Shashanka (Gauda) killed Rajyavardhana
Battle of the Narmada (~618 AD): Pulakeshin II defeated Harsha and took the title Dakshinapatheshvara; Narasimhavarman I defeated him and took the title Vatapikonda
Badami Chalukyas founded by Pulakeshin I; last ruler Kirtivarman II, defeated by Dantidurga (Rashtrakuta); Eastern Chalukya capital Vengi (Kubja Vishnuvardhana), Later Chalukyas at Kalyani
Temple styles: Nagara - Guptas (shikhara, panchayatana, jagati), Dravida - Pallavas (vimana, gopuram), Vesara - Chalukyas; Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh and Bhitargaon brick temple are Gupta-era
Pallavas: founder Simhavishnu, capital Kanchi; Mahendravarman I rock-cut temples, Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) Pancha Rathas, Narasimhavarman II Shore and Kailasanatha temples
Chalukyas: Badami caves, Aihole (Durga Temple), Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal (Lokamahadevi); Kailasa Temple at Ellora (Cave 16) by Rashtrakuta Krishna I
Gupta administration: Bhukti-Uparika, Vishaya-Vishayapati, Grama-Gramika; Kumaramatya, Sandhivigrahika, Mahadandanayaka, Ranabhandagarika, Pilupati
Taxes: Uparikara, Vishti (forced labour), Halivakara, Bhaga (1/6), Hiranya, Chikara (emergency); Tadaga - tank, Prapa - drinking-water shed
Nalanda - Kumaragupta I (destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji), Vikramashila - Dharmapala, Odantapuri - Gopala; Maitraka (Vallabhi) Dronasimha issued a land grant in 502 AD
Buddhist Council patrons: Ajatashatru, Kalashoka, Ashoka, Kanishka; Kushanas issued the purest gold coins, Guptas the largest number

mcqs.e: Brahmadeya was land granted to Brahmins.

mcqs.q: What was the 'Ur' in the Tamil region?
mcqs.e: The Sabha was the assembly of learned Brahmins.

mcqs.q: The 'Sabha' was the assembly of:
mcqs.e: The assembly of common people was the 'Ur'.

mcqs.q: The term 'Tadaga' was used for:
mcqs.e: Prapa was a drinking-water shed.

mcqs.q: What was a 'Prapa'?
mcqs.e: It provided water to all.

mcqs.q: What did the term 'Kshetra' mean in the post-Gupta period?
mcqs.e: Kshetra referred to cultivated fields.

mcqs.q: In which region is Tirabhukti (Tirhut)?
mcqs.e: Present-day north Bihar.

mcqs.q: Which region was called Jejakabhukti?
mcqs.e: The region associated with the Chandelas.

mcqs.q: Which lake was built by Pushyagupta Vaishya and later repaired by Rudradaman?
mcqs.e: Pushyagupta was Chandragupta Maurya's governor.

mcqs.q: Why was Indo-Byzantine trade affected?
o: The Byzantine Empire learned silk production
mcqs.e: So they no longer imported silk from India.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT among the epigraphic sources of Harsha?
mcqs.e: The Banskhera inscription and Nalanda seals relate to Harsha.

mcqs.q: Which wing of the army declined in importance during the Gupta period?
mcqs.e: Cavalry became prominent instead.

mcqs.q: Which wings make up the 'Chaturangini' army?
mcqs.e: The chariot declined while cavalry grew in importance.

mcqs.q: Which title did Pallava kings adopt to show they were guided by the Dharmashastras?
mcqs.e: Maharajadhiraja was taken by Chandragupta I and Ishanavarman.

mcqs.q: What does 'Dakshinapatheshvara', the title of the Chalukya ruler who defeated Harsha, mean?
mcqs.e: This title was taken by Pulakeshin II.
